response.title: Can a battery power station run a window AC all night so we can sleep, or will it die before morning?
response.answer:
Yes, a battery power station can run a window AC all night, but you need a fairly large battery. Most smaller portable power stations will die before morning.

The biggest factors are your AC's power consumption, the battery capacity, and how frequently the AC compressor runs.

How long will a battery run a window AC?

Assuming an 8-hour night, here are realistic estimates for a typical 5,000–8,000 BTU window AC.

Battery capacity

	

Estimated runtime

1–2 hours




2,000 Wh (2 kWh)

	

2–4 hours




3,000 Wh (3 kWh)

	

4–6 hours




5,000 Wh (5 kWh)

	

6–10 hours




7,000 Wh (7 kWh)

	

9–14 hours

Estimates assume roughly 500–800 W average AC consumption, including compressor cycling, and 85% usable battery energy after inverter losses. Actual runtime can vary significantly.

What size battery do you need?
Overnight AC battery calculator

Adjust these values to estimate the battery capacity needed.

AC running power

600 W

Hours of sleep

8 hours

Compressor duty cycle

70%

70% means the AC averages 70% of its running power over the night. Hot weather may push this toward 100%.

Estimated minimum battery capacity

3.95 kWh

For more margin, aim for around 4.7 kWh of rated capacity.

A few important things

Inverter ACs are better: Variable-speed inverter window units can use substantially less energy overnight than traditional fixed-speed models.

Startup surge matters: A traditional compressor can briefly draw much more power when starting. The power station's AC output and surge rating must support it.

Battery size isn't everything: A 2,000 Wh power station with a 300 W AC output still cannot run a 600 W air conditioner.

Keep the battery indoors and dry: Don't block its ventilation, and don't use a gas generator indoors or near windows.

markup:
**Yes, a battery power station can run a window AC all night, but you need a fairly large battery.** Most smaller portable power stations will die before morning.

The biggest factors are your AC's power consumption, the battery capacity, and how frequently the AC compressor runs.

## How long will a battery run a window AC?

Assuming an 8-hour night, here are realistic estimates for a typical 5,000–8,000 BTU window AC.

| Battery capacity | Estimated runtime |
|---|---|
| 500 Wh | 0.5–1 hour |
| 1,000 Wh (1 kWh) | 1–2 hours |
| 2,000 Wh (2 kWh) | 2–4 hours |
| 3,000 Wh (3 kWh) | 4–6 hours |
| 5,000 Wh (5 kWh) | 6–10 hours |
| 7,000 Wh (7 kWh) | 9–14 hours |

<text color="secondary" size="xs">Estimates assume roughly 500–800 W average AC consumption, including compressor cycling, and 85% usable battery energy after inverter losses. Actual runtime can vary significantly.</text>

## What size battery do you need?

<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  {@body const [watts,setWatts] = DIL.useState(600)}
  {@body const [hours,setHours] = DIL.useState(8)}
  {@body const [duty,setDuty] = DIL.useState(70)}
  {@body const needed = Math.ceil(watts*hours*duty/100/0.85)}
  <title size="lg">Overnight AC battery calculator</title>
  <text color="secondary" size="sm">Adjust these values to estimate the battery capacity needed.</text>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    **AC running power**
    <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{watts} W</text>
  </row>
  <slider min={300} max={1500} step={50} value={watts} onChange={setWatts}/>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    **Hours of sleep**
    <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{hours} hours</text>
  </row>
  <slider min={4} max={12} step={1} value={hours} onChange={setHours}/>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    **Compressor duty cycle**
    <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{duty}%</text>
  </row>
  <slider min={30} max={100} step={5} value={duty} onChange={setDuty}/>
  <text color="secondary" size="xs">70% means the AC averages 70% of its running power over the night. Hot weather may push this toward 100%.</text>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">Estimated minimum battery capacity</text>
  <title size="2xl" color="default" tabularNums>{(needed/1000).toFixed(2)} kWh</title>
  <text color="secondary" size="sm">For more margin, aim for around {((needed*1.2)/1000).toFixed(1)} kWh of rated capacity.</text>
</box>

## A few important things

- **Inverter ACs are better:** Variable-speed inverter window units can use substantially less energy overnight than traditional fixed-speed models.
- **Startup surge matters:** A traditional compressor can briefly draw much more power when starting. The power station's AC output and surge rating must support it.
- **Battery size isn't everything:** A 2,000 Wh power station with a 300 W AC output still cannot run a 600 W air conditioner.
- **Keep the battery indoors and dry:** Don't block its ventilation, and don't use a gas generator indoors or near windows.

## Two questions so I can tell you whether it will last all night

{@body const [ac,setAc] = DIL.useState("5000")}
{@body const [battery,setBattery] = DIL.useState("2000")}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <form gap={3} onSubmit={()=>GenUI.issueNewTurn("My window AC is "+ac+" BTU and my battery power station capacity is "+battery+" Wh. Estimate whether it will run for 8 hours overnight, and what power output rating I need.")}>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>1. How big is your window AC?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={ac} onChange={setAc}>
        <radio value="5000">5,000 BTU (small bedroom)</radio>
        <radio value="8000">8,000 BTU (medium bedroom)</radio>
        <radio value="12000">12,000 BTU (large room)</radio>
        <radio value="unknown">Not sure</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>2. How big is your battery?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={battery} onChange={setBattery}>
        <radio value="1000">1,000 Wh / 1 kWh</radio>
        <radio value="2000">2,000 Wh / 2 kWh</radio>
        <radio value="4000">4,000 Wh / 4 kWh</radio>
        <radio value="unknown">Haven't bought one yet</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <button block submit>Estimate my overnight runtime <icon name="arrow-right" inline/></button>
  </form>
</box>

If you know the exact AC model and power station model, I can give you a much more accurate estimate than these general ranges.
